content.comment_body: Hello [product_name] users. I'm encountering an issue with summer/winter time switching. Currently, the automatic changeover isn't working. For the EU, the switch should occur on the last Sunday in March and October. Here’s my process on the [product_name] (tried both manually via display and via PC): 1) I activate summer/winter time (EU setting), 2) I set the correct date and time, 3) I select timezone UTC+1 (Denmark). To test, I set date/time to October 29, 2023 at 02:55. I expect the clock to go back to 02:00 when reaching 03:00, but instead, the clock continues to 03:01 and onwards. Is there something I'm missing?

Hello [user_name], Which version of [product_name] software are you using? Which [product_name] hardware (reference and version) do you have? I found an FAQ: 'How do you switch over to summer or winter time in [product_name] software?' Are you able to configure it as described there?

Thank you for responding. My firmware is version [version_no], and hardware is [product_name] [version_no]. Software is [product_name] [version_no]. The guide you mention shows setting summer/winter time to 'user defined,' but that only allows date entry for one year (2 switch times). I want this to happen automatically every year, which is why I select EU instead of user defined.

Hello [user_name], Thanks for providing the details. I suggest the following test: Set the date and time to October 25, 2023, at 1:59, then wait an hour—at 2:59, the time should jump to 2:00. This helps clarify whether the time change happens correctly, as between 2:00 and 2:59, it's unclear which time zone is active. Additionally, your firmware appears up to date, so that's likely not the issue. You might also try updating to the latest [product_name] software service pack. You can find download and installation instructions at [document]. Hope this helps.
Can you explain why you suggested setting the date to October 25? Or did you mean October 29?

Hi [user_name], If I recall correctly, here the time change happens early morning on October 25 to 26. At least that's the case in my location. Try both dates to see if selecting the wrong day impacts the result.

I suspect the firmware is buggy. Testing on an older [product_name] [version_no], the function works correctly. On newer [product_name] [version_no] and [version_no], the summer/winter time switch does not work.
I haven’t encountered this issue because I synchronize the time on my [product_name] devices using an NTP time server. In my setup, the NTP server is my router (Fritz!Box 7490).

Thank you for your response. Regardless of what I try, the time won’t change automatically, so this could well be a firmware bug. Does anyone have insights on if there’s a planned fix or timeline? I’ll look into NTP. If I set up NTP, I assume I’ll need a server that handles summer/winter time changes, otherwise [product_name] will just read time from the server and won’t switch on its own. Any recommendations for reliable NTP servers?

For summer/winter time changes, the setting on [product_name] still needs to be active. Why the switch works with an NTP server and not independently, I’m not sure. I use my Fritz!Box as an NTP server, so I don’t have another specific recommendation.
Here’s a website you can check: pool.ntp.org: NTP Servers in Denmark, dk.pool.ntp.org ([url])
I ran another test on [product_name] [version_no]. This time, I set the date to October 29, 2023, at 1:58 AM. The result: the reset to winter time occurred as expected.
Confirmed with a test here as well, it appears to work now. Thank you for your assistance and time.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report difficulties with automatic summer/winter time change using EU settings on [product_name] hardware paired with [product_name] software. Even with proper time, date, and timezone configuration, the feature doesn’t trigger as expected on versions [version_no], while older hardware works correctly. Testing and discussion suggest this may be due to a firmware issue impacting reliable automation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to switch time automatically for summer/winter changes in line with the EU schedule each year, without manual adjustments, and to function reliably with the EU setting.
